Project Description: The Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy Temple is an ancient Hindu temple constructed in the 17th century and a reckoned pilgrim centre in Tiruchendur, Tamil Nadu. The Subramaniya Swamy Temple is under the control of the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) Department, Government of Tamil Nadu. The temple is situated close to the shoreline facing the Bay of Bengal. The eastern side of compound wall of the temple and Valli Kugai is located close to the shoreline. The temple eastern side compound wall and the Valli Kugai is facing sea erosion due to the waves breaking on the structure. In order to prevent the eastern side of the temple and Valli Kugai from the erosion, a sea wall was built in the year 1968 – 69. The sea wall undergoes sliding and it is periodically repaired. Presently, it is proposed to repair and reconstruct the shore protection seawall with the Gabion arrangement as suggested by IIT Madras.

Project Description: The proposed project is construction of storm drain channel with culvert bridges at Aruva Mooku region of Paravanar River originates from Perumal tank in Chidambaram and traverses north parallel to the coast. It undergoes meandering and takes an OX shape to a distance of 1 km towards the coast near Aruva Mooku. The OX shape meandering falls 1.6 km close to sea. During the cyclones and peak monsoon seasons, the villages along the Paravanar River gets flooded due to excess rainwater opened from Perumal Lake. The excess rainfall during monsoon triggers flood in Paravanar River near Aruva Mooku region. In order to discharge excess flood water into the adjoining Bay of Bengal in Cuddalore district, Tamil Nadu, PWD has proposed to construct a storm drain channel with associated facilities from Aruva Mooku, Paravanar River to Bay of Bengal. The technical aspects of the project have been done by IIT Madras and given the design and recommended for the implementation. It is for public welfare.

Project Description: As assessed, Geological Reserves of Lime Kankar in the Lease is 43,68,788 Tonnes and Mineable Reserves is 30,71,388 Tonnes. The quarried Lime Kankar will be transported by 25 T Tarus Tippers to Pandalgudi Lime Kankar Beneficiation Plant for further process. Black Cotton Top Soil will be transported by 25 T Tarus Tippers to RR Nagar Cement Plant for utilizing as corrective material in Cement manufacturing. The proposed Pumped Storage Project will be situated between the Upper Bhavani Reservoir at the upstream and the Avalanche Dam at the downstream. There will be no additional submergence of land in the proposed Pumped Storage Project as both the reservoirs already exist. Project Description: The Ulakkaruviar Reservoir Project envisages construction of a dam across River Ulakkaruviar to mitigate flood problems in the Pazhayar Sub-Basin and provide irrigation and domestic water supply. The project includes: (i) An earthen dam 1.777 km long with maximum height of 48.5 m creating storage capacity of 11.97 MCM at FRL 109.0 m; (ii) A 38 m wide ogee-type spillway with discharge capacity of 475 cumecs with 4 bays; (iii) River sluice at chainage 920.0 m with 1000 cusecs capacity; (iv) Canal sluice at chainage 880.0 m with 50 cusecs capacity to feed Thovalai Channel; (v) Lined canal system. The project will provide irrigation to 7,000 ha Cultural Command Area (CCA), supply 1.23 MCM for domestic water consumption, and mitigate 20% of flood damages in Pazhayar Basin (estimated annual savings Rs. 25-30 Crore). The catchment area is 15.745 sq km. The project cost is Rs. 2,045 Crore at 2024-25 price level with a Benefit-Cost Ratio of 1.33, indicating economic viability.

Project Description:
Kannathur (Kanathur) Reddykuppam Village in Thiruporur Taluk, Chengalpattu District, Tamil Nadu, is a traditional fishing village with about 938 fishermen operating nearly 138 outboard motorized boats. Marine fishing is the primary livelihood source, and the district recorded about 13,023.37 tonnes of marine fish production during 2014–15. The existing Fish Landing Centre (FLC) lacks essential infrastructure such as net-mending sheds, internal roads, and sanitation facilities.
Most of the earlier facilities have been damaged due to continuous coastal erosion.
There is no designated berthing or safe anchoring facility, and boats are directly beached along the open shore. This exposes fishing crafts to severe damage during rough sea conditions, high waves, and cyclonic events. The coastal stretch is facing persistent shoreline erosion, leading to loss of settlements and infrastructure. Considering the severe erosion and livelihood risks, shoreline protection measures are urgently needed.

Project Description: Process involves feeding of ROM Lime Kankar from captive Kankar quarries to Hoppers. The mineral is crushed to required size in a Twin Shaft Sizer / Crusher. The material is then conveyed to rotary Wet Scrubbers and water is added. Required water demand is met from abandoned mine pits and there is no ground water tapping.  By combined action of attrition & scrubbing, adherent Clay and Silica contents are washed away from Kankar. Washed Clean Kankar is transported to Cement Plant. Undersize material is pumped to Hydro Cyclones for de-sliming. The dewatered oversize material is ‘Sub Grade Kankar’ and is also dispatched to Cement Plant. Water separated and collected from Screens are pumped to Thickeners for settling. Clarified water is recycled and reused in the Process. Wet Rejects is directly pumped as Tailing slurry through pipeline to mined out voids for backfilling. Settled water from the pit is transported back by return pipeline for reuse in the Process.
